# dsh-plugin-qq-bridge
Bridge an official **QQ bot** to **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** — in-process.
A message in QQ starts (or resumes) a real DSH session **inside the host process**. The session show

s up
in the desktop app's sidebar, can be opened and continued there, and the answer goes back to QQ

as text,
image or file. QQ is just one more input/output for a normal DSH session.
## How it works
| | Separate bridge process | This plugin |
| Task execution | spawns `dsh --profile qq --json` | `ctx.agents.create()` / `resume()` inside the

host |
| Where sessions live | only in that CLI profile | the host's own session store (visible in t

he GUI) |
| Permissions | env vars on the child process | per-session permission preset |
| Lifetime
| you keep `start-bridge.cmd` running | lives as long as the DSH host |
The QQ protocol layer (token, gateway, passive-reply budget, chunking, workspaces, chat history) is

shared
with the standalone bridge; only the execution side is different.
## Requirements

- A DSH host that provides the `agents`, `agentDefaultModel`, `agentPresets`, `permissionPresets`,
`

sessionTitle` and `workspaceRegistry` services (the desktop app does).
- A QQ official bot applicati

on (AppID + AppSecret) with the message intents you plan to use enabled
(C2C, group @-message, …) on
the QQ open platform.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart the DSH host** — host-side plugin code is only loaded at startup.
## Configure

Config lives at `<DSH_HOME>/qq-bridge/config.json` (`~/.dsh/qq-bridge/config.json` by default).
Set
`QQ_BRIDGE_HOME` to point the whole plugin at another directory (handy for testing).
A minimal config:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
See `config.example.json` for every key.
Keys that matter for the plugin:
| Key | Meaning |

| `appId`, `appSecret` | QQ bot credentials (from the QQ open platform). |
| `sandbox` | Use the QQ

sandbox environment instead of production. |
| `intents` | Message subscription bitmask; `33554432`

is C2C messages, add the group bit for group chats. |
| `defaultCwd` | Working directory for new ses
sions. Point it at a registered DSH workspace to have QQ sessions appear there; leave empty for an i

solated directory per session. |
| `agentPreset` | Agent preset name; empty means the host default.

|
| `permissionPreset` | `danger-full-access` (default, unattended), `workspace-write` or `read-only

`. |
| `attachWorkspace` | When `defaultCwd` is a registered workspace, attach the session to it so

the GUI shows it. |
| `allow.users` / `allow.groups` | OpenID allow-lists. Empty means "locked": use

`/bind <code>` with `bindCode` to pair. |
| `maxConcurrent`, `queueLimit` | How many agent runs at

once, how many conversations may queue. |
| `passiveWindowMs` | The passive-reply window QQ gives yo

u after a user message. |
| `taskTimeoutMs` | Per-task timeout. |
| `selfTestOnBoot` | Run one end-t

o-end self test on first boot and post the result to QQ. |
| `titlePrefix` | Session title prefix (d

on first boot and post the result to QQ. |
| `titlePrefix` | Session title prefix (default `QQ`). |
## Commands (sent in QQ)

`/help`, `/id`, `/bind <code>`, `/new`, `/status`, `/stop`,
`/ws` (list workspaces), `/ws <name|inde

x>`, `/ws 0` (back to the default directory),
`/history [n]`.
## Files
Everything the plugin writes lives under `<QQ_BRIDGE_HOME>` (default `<DSH_HOME>/qq-bridge`):

`config.json`, `state.json` (session map, allow-lists), `history/` (per session and workspace),
`wor
kspaces/` (workspace link index), `tasks/` (default task root) and `logs/`.
## Security note
The default `permissionPreset` is `danger-full-access` so an unattended QQ task can actually do its

job.
Set it to `workspace-write` or `read-only` if the bot is reachable by anyone you do not trust,

and keep
`allow.users` limited to people you know.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Set `QQ_BRIDGE_HOME` to a scratch directory so the mock run does not touch real data.
